title: The pen or the keyboard
text: Laptops let students take notes faster than any pen — so why does research keep {{1}} that handwriting serves learning better? When students type, the speed {{2}} verbatim transcription: they can capture every word, and studies show many do, transcribing lectures like court reporters. Writing by hand is {{3}}, and the constraint {{4}} the note-taker to summarise, select and rephrase — to process the material in order to fit it on the page. That extra processing is the {{5}}. In classic experiments, students who took handwritten notes answered conceptual questions about a lecture better than typists did, even though typists {{6}} more facts in the moment; the typists' detailed notes did not {{7}} the deficit, presumably because their notes recorded the lecture without ever reaching the understanding. The effect survives the obvious objections: it appears whether or not students study their notes afterwards, which {{8}} that the benefit comes from forming the notes, not rereading them. None of this makes the laptop the villain — for recording data, searching text or sharing work, the keyboard wins easily. But for turning a lecture into learning, slower turns out to be a feature, not a bug.

gaps.explanation: 'research keeps finding that…' — 'keep' takes the gerund; the other forms break the grammar of 'keeps ___ that'.
'the speed invites verbatim transcription' — makes it tempting; inhibit = hold back, which reverses the meaning.
'writing by hand is slower' — takes more time; 'lower' is for height or amount, 'lesser' for importance.
'the constraint forces the note-taker to summarise' — compels them to; forge = fake or forge ahead, forfeit = lose a right.
'that extra processing is the secret' — the hidden cause of success; sequel = a continuation of a story.
'typists captured more facts in the moment' — recorded them; cart = carry clumsily by vehicle.
'did not repair the deficit' — make good the shortfall; repeal = cancel a law, repay = give money back.
'which implies that the benefit comes from forming the notes' — points to that conclusion; supply = provide, apply takes 'to'.
